title: I Set the Lord Before My Face
description: I Set the Lord Before My Face in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 16, part 5, headed “The death and resurrection of Christ”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: I Set the Lord be-fore my face, "He bears my cou-rage up; "My heart, and tongue, their joys ex-press, "My flesh shall rest in hope.

lines: I Set the Lord before my face,
"My heart, and tongue, their joys express,
"My spirit, Lord, thou wilt not leave
"Nor quit my body to the grave
"Thou wilt reveal the path of life,
Thus in the name of Christ, the Lord,
Behold the tomb its prey restores,
When shall my feet arise and stand
There sits the Son at God's right hand,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
